title: Ephemeral 1 fF cells for millisecond-lifetime AI activations
idea: TRIZ #27 Cheap short-living objects: build sub-arrays whose cells hold only ~1 fF and keep data ~1-5 ms with no refresh at all, reserved for activations and KV tiles that are written once and consumed within a millisecond. The compiler tags data lifetimes, and the controller rejects stale reads by timestamp.
why: Facts 1 and 3: capacitor 4-5x smaller (AR ~15:1), zero refresh energy, ~2x density for transient data.

title: Mitochondrial nano-battery bit: emf read by a high-impedance gain transistor
idea: Mitochondria store energy as an electrochemical gradient, not as free charge. Put a 20 nm solid-state micro-battery (LixTiO2 | thin solid electrolyte | LixMnO2) on each gain-transistor gate. The bit is the electrode state of charge, which sets an open-circuit voltage ~0.3-0.5 V apart, read with no current drawn.
why: Non-volatile like a battery (months), yet read non-destructively in ns. Chemical potential replaces capacitance, so there is no capacitor wall, and writes below 1 V attack the voltage floor (fact 10).

title: Charge-density-wave electron-crystal bit in 1T-TaS2 nanoflakes
idea: Scarcity rule: no atom may move during a write. Store the bit as the electronic order of a 1T-TaS2 (or strain-stabilized analog) island: a ~ps current pulse switches the insulating commensurate CDW into a metallic hidden CDW state, a longer weak pulse restores it, and read uses the ~10x resistance contrast. Only the electron lattice rearranges, so there is no ionic fatigue.
why: Targets unlimited endurance with ps, fJ-class writes in a 2-terminal crosspoint element, sidestepping the CV2 floor (fact 10); room-temperature stability of the hidden state is the open physics question.

title: Power-grid thyristor shrunk to a 15 nm memory pillar
idea: Scale shift from grid-scale SCRs to a 15 nm vertical pnpn pillar: regenerative bipolar feedback latches the cell on or off, a gate pulse switches it, and a small holding bias keeps it, giving a 4F2 capacitor-free cell.
why: Density and process: 4F2 with no capacitor etch, fast read current 10x DRAM.

title: Telescoping nanotube bit: storage as superlubric shell position
idea: Rearrange the bit into geometry: the inner shell of a double-wall carbon nanotube slides in or out of its outer shell (a wear-free superlubric van der Waals bearing) between two electrostatic detents; in the out position it tunnels to a contact, so read is current on/off and write is a ns electrostatic pull.
why: Refresh and endurance (fact 3): no charge to leak, near-zero-wear sliding aims at unlimited cycles in a ~10 nm footprint; risk is deterministic nanotube placement.

title: Zn: indium-free zinc-tin-oxide gain cell stores three bits per node
idea: Use a ZnSnO (no In, no Ga) two-transistor gain cell whose ultralow off-current holds 8 charge levels on the read-transistor gate; level spacing is squeezed until ~1% of symbols land one level off, which a Gray-coded soft-decision LDPC per row corrects.
why: Three bits per cell triple density with no capacitor (facts 1, 2) and avoid scarce indium and gallium; the 1% tolerance is what makes 8 levels possible on a noisy oxide channel.

title: Sn: back-end complementary oxide latch from p-SnO and n-ZnO
idea: Stack a cross-coupled four-transistor latch of p-type SnO and n-type ZnO thin-film transistors in the back-end wiring, tens of tiers high; the latch needs no refresh, and SnO's poor hole mobility and variability are allowed to create ~1% weak cells that a row code corrects.
why: Static, refresh-free storage (fact 3) stacked in 3D at <=400 C over logic using abundant metals; accepting weak p-channel devices is what makes oxide CMOS usable as memory.

title: Optane's crosspoint kept, PCM swapped for selector-gated capacitor
idea: Optane died largely on cost and PCM endurance, but its stacked crosspoint and OTS selector worked. Place a tiny MIM capacitor in series with the OTS at each crosspoint: the selector's threshold snap acts as a transistor-free access device, turning the array into a refreshed 4F2 multi-deck DRAM.
why: 4F2 per deck with stackable decks and no lateral transistor (Fact 2); reuses idle chalcogenide PVD tooling. Risk: OTS sub-threshold leakage must reach ~fA.

title: Fe: bacteria-grown greigite magnetosomes self-assemble into magnetic bit arrays
idea: Harvest near-monodisperse 40-80 nm Fe3S4 (greigite) magnetosomes from magnetotactic bacteria and dock them by magnetic self-assembly into a pre-patterned spin-orbit-torque crossbar, one particle per site; the ~1% of sites left empty or doubly filled are mapped out as erasures.
why: Bio-fabricated storage elements grown at room temperature with no lithography for the bit itself (fact 4), from abundant Fe and S; docking accuracy and read speed are major unknowns.

title: O: single oxide-trap occupancy in a tiny FinFET as bit
idea: Use the random-telegraph trap that ultra-scaled transistors carry: one oxide trap near the channel whose occupancy shifts Vt by ~20-50 mV; set it with a gate bias, read via drain current, map out devices without a usable trap at test, and accept ~1% thermal flips per refresh window.
why: Atomic-scale storage inside a minimal transistor with no capacitor (facts 1, 4), turning device noise into a bit; only viable because 1% stochastic capture errors are allowed.

title: Thin-film battery plateau: two-phase lithium node holds voltage despite leakage
idea: A battery's flat voltage plateau barely moves as charge leaks, unlike a capacitor's linear droop; make each node a ~50-nm solid-state nanobattery (sputtered Li4Ti5O12 or LiFePO4 electrode, ~10-nm Li3PS4 or LiPON electrolyte) whose states are the charged and discharged plateaus, sensed by a gain transistor; ~1e5 stored Li+ outlast fA leakage.
why: Fact 3: at the 13 fA tail, 1e5 charges last ~1 s (~20x the refresh window) while the voltage stays digital, never drifting into the sense margin; buildable with sputter, evaporator and a glovebox; ionic write speed and cycle life are the risks.

title: Re-meltable tin-bismuth plate fill replaces tungsten and drains out
idea: TRIZ #29 Hydraulics + #36 Phase transition: pressure-infiltrate molten Sn-Bi eutectic (139 C) over a wetting liner to fill capacitor interiors and the common plate instead of CVD W/TiN. It is solid in service, can be reflowed to heal voids, and is melted out at end of life for direct reuse.
why: Tungsten chokepoint (China ~80%) and recyclability; avoids WF6 fluorine damage; ~100 MPa Laplace pressure for 10-nm pores is the risk.

title: Wurtzite AlScN ferroelectric delivers planar 11,000-electron bits
idea: Sputter Al0.7Sc0.3N at <=400 C, thinned to ~5 nm to keep coercive voltage near 2 V. Its 2Pr ~ 200 uC/cm2 delivers ~1.8 fC (~11,000 e) from a flat 30x30 nm capacitor, versus ~0.1 fC from a dielectric, in a 1T1C destructive-read cell with no high-AR pillar.
why: Polarization charge density, not k*E, breaks the charge wall (fact 1) and removes the 60-75:1 etch. Endurance (1e6-1e8 today) is the key risk, to fix by electrode and strain engineering.

title: Conductive ferroelectric domain wall bit read by current
idea: IFR: read the bit without disturbing it. Closest achievable: in a thin LiNbO3 or BiFeO3 mesa a write pulse creates or erases a charged domain wall between two side electrodes; reading passes a small current only when the conductive wall exists, leaving polarization untouched.
why: Fact 8: nondestructive read removes restore energy and permits small fetch granules; nonvolatile so no refresh; domains switch in sub-ns.

title: Harvest and re-bin DRAM dies from retired server DIMMs
idea: MAGNIFY the life of existing storage elements: a small reverse-logistics shop buys decommissioned DDR4 DIMMs, retention-tests every die at elevated temperature, re-bins by refresh class and rebuilds CXL memory expanders whose controller applies per-die refresh rates.
why: Raises usable supply without new wafers during the shortage; cost per bit near scrap value plus test.

title: Open-source DRAM-cell library on US foundry PDKs
idea: Worsen: keep storage-cell know-how locked inside three companies. Flip: spend $1M over 24 months designing, taping out and publishing open-source eDRAM and gain cells (thick-oxide 3T, MIM 1T1C) on SkyWater 130 and 22FDX PDKs with measured retention data, so any US chip team can add dense memory.
why: U.S. manufacturability and supply diversification; lowers the entry cost for new memory makers.

title: Swap plasma etching for metal-assisted chemical etching of deep trenches
idea: Pattern a Pt or Ag catalyst mesh by DUV (or by dewetting) and immerse it in HF/H2O2. The catalyst sinks straight into the silicon, cutting vertical holes with AR above 200:1 and no plasma damage, and ALD MIM lines them as IBM-style deep-trench storage capacitors under the access transistor.
why: ~3x the AR of today's pillars gives ~3x Cs (fact 1), or the same Cs at a relaxed DUV diameter, with no EUV and a cheap wet bench instead of high-power etch tools (fact 4).

title: AlN-clad GaN quantum-well storage node with barrier-tilting write
idea: MAGNIFY the confining barrier from ~1 eV (Si junction) to ~2 eV by holding the bit as electrons in a 3-nm GaN well clad with AlN; a transfer gate transiently tilts the barrier with the help of the built-in polarization field (CCD-style transfer) to write in ~5 ns, and a HEMT channel beneath the well senses the stored charge non-destructively.
why: Thermionic escape falls by ~e^(-1 eV/kT) ~1e-17, so retention moves from 64 ms to hours and refresh (fact 3: 16-33% idle power, 10-20% bandwidth) nearly vanishes; no oxide tunneling, so endurance stays unlimited.

title: Pencil lead: carbon mold capacitors released by dry ash, no HF
idea: Stimulus 'pencil lead' -> build the capacitor mold from amorphous carbon instead of oxide, etch holes with O2/SO2 plasma, deposit the electrodes, then remove the mold by oxygen ashing. Today the oxide mold is stripped in liquid HF whose capillary forces topple tall cylinders; a dry ash has no capillary force at all.
why: Removes the pattern-collapse limit so pillars can reach the ~115:1 AR needed for more charge (fact 1); eliminates HF and C4F8 from the capacitor module with existing tools.

title: Po: memory printed like a newspaper — roll-to-roll nanoimprinted oxide cells
idea: Po: memory is printed like a newspaper. Extracted: roll-to-roll nanoimprint 50 nm features onto steel or polyimide foil, with spatial-ALD oxide channels and planar capacitors, making 1T1C arrays on a 1 m web; the slower cells sit behind a small silicon cache.
why: Processed DRAM silicon costs on the order of $100k/m2 vs ~$10-50/m2 for R2R, so even at ~17x lower density cost per bit can fall 100x+. Overlay accuracy on a moving web is the key risk.

title: Optical wordlines: photoconductor-gated storage nodes, no access transistor
idea: Reverse the wordline's role from voltage to light: each storage capacitor reaches its bitline through a nanoscale amorphous-selenium/chalcogenide photoconductor (dark resistivity >1e14 ohm-cm), and a row is selected by a ~1 ns light pulse in a SiN waveguide running under it. In the dark the node is isolated by an insulator rather than a leaky transistor.
why: Attacks the access-transistor leakage tail (fact 3) and wordline coupling/voltage (facts 9,10): dark-current-limited retention of seconds (>=30x fewer refreshes), no 3 V electrical wordline swing, and no capacitive row hammer.

title: Two-faced wafer: capacitors built on the thinned backside
idea: Borrow the wafer-scale backside-power trick: after front-side transistor and bitline processing, bond to a carrier, thin to 1 um and build the capacitor stack on the backside, connected by nano-vias through vertical access transistors, so capacitors no longer compete with bitlines and contacts.
why: Density and process: frees ~30-40% of front-side cell area and lets capacitors use full-cell footprint; enables 4F2 vertical-channel cells.

title: Hundred-electron bits read by room-temperature single-electron transistors
idea: Invert 'a bit needs ~30,000 stored electrons' -> store ~100. Each node is a ~20 aF floating island sensed by a single-electron transistor built from a ~1.5 nm metal cluster or molecule, whose Coulomb oscillations turn +/-100 electrons into a large current swing.
why: Eliminates the capacitor (fact 1) and cuts write energy to ~1.6e-17 J (~1000x, fact 10) at ~4F^2; room-temperature SET uniformity is the speculative part.

title: Charged microring junction: bits read by wavelength, not bitlines
idea: Worsen: read every bit through a long, power-hungry copper bitline. Flip: on a ~$60k silicon-photonics shuttle, store each bit as charge on the depletion capacitance of a microring's PN junction, which shifts its resonance, so one waveguide reads 32-64 bits in parallel by wavelength; demonstrated within 24 months.
why: Data-movement energy (fact 5) and sense-amp periphery (fact 7), with optical readout next to the accelerator.

title: Coaxial pillar: storage capacitor core inside vertical transistor shell
idea: Fuse access transistor and capacitor into one vertical pillar: a grounded TiN core plate, a high-k sleeve, and a doped-oxide storage-node shell form the capacitor, and the same shell continues upward as a short vertical channel gated by a wordline ring at the pillar top. The capacitor uses the pillar volume and the transistor uses the pillar skin, so one pillar is one 4F2 cell with no landing pad.
why: Density 6F2 to 4F2 (+33% bits/area) and removes the storage-node contact and landing-pad litho layers; attacks facts 2 and 4.

title: Archimedes' lever: negative-capacitance ferroelectric boosts storage capacitor
idea: An ancient Greek engineer would add a lever rather than a longer arm. Put a thin ferroelectric, stabilized in its negative-capacitance branch, in series with the ZrO2/Al2O3 storage dielectric so the stack's effective capacitance exceeds that of the dielectric alone, reaching an effective k>100 in today's pillar.
why: Hits the k~70 target of fact 1 without going to AR 115: ~2x Cs, or the same Cs from half the pillar height with fewer etch and deposition steps (fact 4).

title: One skyrmion per nanodisk: topological winding number as the bit
idea: Effect walk: Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya chiral magnetism. A 20-nm Ta/CoFeB/MgO disk holds zero or one skyrmion; a current pulse nucleates or annihilates it at an engineered notch, and the bit is read through noncollinear magnetoresistance in a vertical tunnel stack.
why: Topological winding adds an energy barrier that does not scale with volume, so retention holds at smaller volumes than an MTJ free layer, pushing density past MRAM's thermal-stability limit.

title: Indium- and gallium-free zinc-silicon-oxide gain cell from domestic zinc
idea: Box = {medium: charge on the gate node of a read transistor | access: amorphous Zn-Si-O write TFT (wide gap, ultralow off-current) | sense: gain-cell read current | integration: 4-8 monolithic BEOL tiers | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: ALD with zinc from Alaska + U.S. silane}. Si suppresses oxygen vacancies in ZnO the way Ga does in IGZO, aiming for aA-level off-current without indium (mostly imported) or gallium (~98% Chinese).
why: Scarce resources and U.S. manufacturability: removes In and Ga from oxide-semiconductor DRAM while keeping long retention and 3D tiers.

title: Voltage-only magnetoelectric cell read by inverse Rashba-Edelstein voltage
idea: Effect walk: magnetoelectric coupling + spin-to-charge conversion. A 10-nm La-doped BiFeO3 film reorients its canted antiferromagnetic order at ~100 mV, dragging an exchange-coupled CoFe nanomagnet; reading passes a tiny spin current into a Bi/Ag or topological interface whose inverse Rashba-Edelstein effect outputs a voltage whose sign is the bit.
why: Write is capacitive (~10 aJ at 100 mV, no charge current) and read is non-destructive, aiming 10-100x below DRAM's fJ-class cell+bitline write and restore energy (facts 8, 10).

title: Recirculating GHz phonon loops revive mercury delay-line memory on chip
idea: Effect walk: piezoelectric transduction of acoustic waves. Bits are 100-ps acoustic pulses circulating in a thin-film LiNbO3-on-Si phononic waveguide loop, regenerated once per lap by a piezo transducer and amplifier; slow-wave phononic-crystal sections (group velocity <200 m/s) pack more bits per micron.
why: A lithography-light, capacitor-free store for sequential data such as KV-cache streams; density is 10-50x below DRAM unless slow-wave sections succeed, so it targets a streaming tier and capital intensity, not random access.

title: Parametron reborn: bits as oscillation phase in pumped nanoresonators
idea: Goto's parametron died because its ferrite-core resonators were big and power-hungry next to transistors. Use GHz AlN nanomechanical resonators parametrically driven by one shared global pump: each holds a 0 or pi oscillation phase indefinitely while the pump runs, is written by a tiny seed pulse and is read by phase comparison.
why: Volatile but leakage-free, so there is no refresh tail (Fact 3) and no row-hammer charge coupling (Fact 9); retention is set by pump stability, not femtoamp leakage. Density limited (~0.1 um2).

title: Breathing lung: brownmillerite oxide inhales oxygen to switch whole-volume
idea: Stimulus 'lungs' -> a 10 nm SrFeO2.5 brownmillerite layer topotactically 'inhales' oxygen from an adjacent Ta2O5 reservoir under +1 V to become metallic SrFeO3, and exhales it at -1 V; the whole volume switches (not a filament), giving ~1000x resistance change with tight cell-to-cell spread.
why: Volume switching removes the variability tail of filamentary ReRAM while staying nonvolatile with no refresh (fact 3); iron-based oxides deposited without fluorine.

title: Charge-density-wave hidden state in tantalum disulfide as bit
idea: IFR: a bit stored in the electron crystal itself. Closest achievable: in thin 1T-TaS2 a ps-to-ns voltage pulse switches the commensurate charge-density wave into a metastable mosaic metallic state and a longer pulse restores it; read is the ~10x resistance change.
why: fJ-scale switching with no capacitor (fact 1) and no ion migration, so endurance is high; needs the hidden state stabilized at room temperature.

title: Magnetic core memory reborn as 100 nm nanorings
idea: Shrink 1950s ferrite cores from mm to nm: CoFe nanorings store the bit as clockwise or counterclockwise vortex chirality, written by coincident current pulses in vertical through-wires and read by an embedded MTJ.
why: Endurance and stray-field-free density: flux-closure chirality is immune to neighbors; no capacitor and nonvolatile.

title: Layer cake: lateral capacitors carved by HCl vapor in Si/SiGe stacks
idea: Stimulus 'layer cake' -> grow a 32-tier Si/SiGe superlattice, cut one vertical slot with Cl2/HBr, recess the SiGe layers sideways with highly selective HCl vapor to form horizontal pockets, and line each pocket with chloride-ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN to make lateral capacitors stacked like cake layers.
why: Delivers the 26+ tiers needed for 3D DRAM breakeven (fact 2) with one litho step for many tiers (fact 4), with no fluorocarbon etch and no HF.

title: Dam: GaN/AlGaN potential well holds stored charge for days
idea: Stimulus 'hydro dam' (water held behind a tall wall) -> store the bit as electrons in an AlGaN/GaN 2DEG pocket behind a 3.4 eV-gap barrier and read it through a gain transistor; leakage falls exponentially with bandgap, so retention reaches hours to days. GaN is grown by MOCVD and etched with Cl2/BCl3, with no fluorine.
why: Shrinks the leakage tail >1000x vs silicon (fact 3) so refresh becomes rare; capacitorless gain-cell read (fact 1).

title: Chill commodity DDR5 to minus 40 C and stretch refresh
idea: Worsen: run memory hot beside 1 kW accelerators, where leakage doubles every ~10 C. Flip: build a $1M pilot of sealed two-phase-cooled DDR5 RDIMMs held at -40 C, where storage-node junction leakage drops ~100x, program the controller for 16x longer refresh intervals, and qualify within 24 months.
why: Refresh energy and bandwidth on existing chips right away (fact 3: recovers most of the 10-20% bandwidth tax).

title: Type-II superlattice storage separates electrons from holes
idea: Adapt infrared-detector InAs/GaSb type-II superlattices (in Si/SiGe or oxide analogues): electrons and holes sit in spatially separated adjacent wells, so each site holds an independent electron bit and hole bit with recombination suppressed by the gap, in 5 tiers.
why: 10x at same cost: 2 bits per site x epitaxially defined tiers is ~10x per footprint; ambipolar read through separate n and p sense paths.

title: Conductive ferroelectric domain walls repurpose U.S. lithium niobate photonics fabs
idea: Telecom photonics users already run thin-film lithium niobate lines; one mask adds electrode pairs on LNOI so writing a domain creates a charged, conductive domain wall between them, read non-destructively by its 1e3-1e5 current contrast without switching polarization.
why: Non-destructive read (fact 8), non-volatile, ns writes on existing U.S. photonics capacity (manufacturability); domain-wall reliability below 50 nm is the risk.

title: One-million-dollar Bit Prize judged on a standard test chip
idea: Worsen: let only incumbents with billion-dollar fabs propose storage elements. Flip: put the full $1M into a 24-month open prize: any storage element that hits 20 ns write, 1e15 cycles and 1 s retention on a supplied standard probe-card test vehicle wins, judged on measured data.
why: Leverages ~10-100x the budget in outside R&D effort and surfaces new storage physics fast.

title: Self-clearing capacitor electrodes from metallized film capacitors
idea: Copy metallized-film capacitors that self-heal: use a 2 nm oxidizable top electrode (TiN/Al) so a one-time wafer-level clearing pulse makes each weak spot in the high-k burn its local electrode into insulator, deleting that leakage path.
why: Facts 1 and 3: removes extrinsic tail bits and lets the dielectric thin ~20%, giving ~25% more Cs at the same aspect ratio.

title: Write-once-per-session charge-trap cells for append-only AI KV caches
idea: KV caches are appended once per token, read thousands of times and discarded at session end, so each location sees ~1e4-1e6 writes per lifetime, not 1e15. Bits are electrons in a thin SiN/Al2O3 trap layer programmed by 50-100 ns channel-hot-electron pulses, bulk-erased per page at session end and read non-destructively by threshold sensing.
why: Charge-trap cells are 4F2 and 3D-stackable with no capacitor (facts 1-2), no refresh and non-destructive read (fact 8): ~5-10x density vs DRAM for this extreme workload, with endurance demand matched by write rarity.

title: Po: the bit is one hydrogen away — proton-intercalation conductance cell
idea: Po: the bit is a hydrogen atom that moved next door. Extracted: a 3-terminal cell drives protons from a thin hydrated reservoir (HfO2:H or a solid acid) into a WO3 channel, changing its conductance >100x; the lightest ion moves in ns at ~0.5 V and retention is tuned by the reservoir bias.
why: Sub-1 V writes break the voltage floor (fact 10) and gain-style read avoids destructive sensing (fact 8). Hydrogen management in CMOS is the risk.

title: Van der Waals adhesion-latched printed nanocantilever bit
idea: IFR: turn stiction, the classic MEMS failure, into the memory. Closest achievable: nanoimprint a cantilever over a printed electrode coated with an anti-wear monolayer; once pulled in, van der Waals adhesion holds it on until a reverse electrostatic or thermal pulse releases it.
why: Zero retention power and nonvolatile; printable via imprint plus sacrificial layer; contact endurance is the risk.

title: Thinfilm polymer FeRAM fixed: proton-transfer organic ferroelectric crystals
idea: Thin Film Electronics' and Intel's PVDF polymer FeRAM died from microsecond switching, half-select disturb and a low Curie point. Grow croconic-acid-type hydrogen-bonded crystals in BEOL vias: they switch by collective proton transfer along H-bond chains (P ~20-30 uC/cm2) and deposit below 150 C, so many tiers can stack.
why: Lead-free nonvolatile layer with a tiny thermal budget for monolithic multi-tier stacks; fast proton switching makes FeRAM DRAM-class.

title: Eliminate holding energy: van der Waals stiction latches nanocantilever bits
idea: Eliminate any energy source for holding state: a 10-nm graphene or ALD-TiN cantilever is pulled electrostatically onto a pad where van der Waals adhesion keeps it stuck (bit 1) with zero power, and a second pull-off electrode peels it free (bit 0); contact resistance reads the state. The sacrificial ALD oxide is removed by vapor HF, so no rare gases are used.
why: Turns the classic MEMS failure, stiction, into the storage mechanism: nonvolatile, leak-free and refresh-free (fact 3); risks are adhesion variability and contact endurance.

title: Protonic shuttle cell stores protons, not electrons
idea: Invert 'the stored carrier is an electron' -> store protons. A 5 nm phosphorus-doped SiO2 solid acid lets protons shuttle under ~1 V/nm pulses into or out of an Nb2O5 or WO3 nano-channel in nanoseconds, setting a non-volatile conductance; protons intercalate without breaking host bonds, the hoped route to near-unlimited endurance.
why: Refresh-free, non-destructive read, ~fJ writes (facts 3, 8, 10); Nb2O5 option avoids the tungsten chokepoint; risk is proving >1e15-cycle endurance.

title: Printed charge-coupled shift-register memory with no per-bit transistor
idea: IFR: memory with zero transistors per bit. Closest achievable: print clocked electrode rows on a continuous oxide-semiconductor film so charge packets shift CCD-style along short lanes to a single sense node per lane; many short lanes keep latency near 100 ns.
why: Facts 7 and 4: removes per-cell access devices and most periphery; only printed electrodes needed, so capital and lithography collapse.

title: Polyoxometalate multi-electron clusters as quantized storage nodes
idea: Adapt polyoxometalate catalysts, which reversibly accept 2-6 electrons at sharp molecule-defined potentials: graft a monolayer of W18-type POMs onto a buried node electrode so each node holds discrete charge states read through a gain transistor.
why: Density and fact 1: molecule-defined charge levels give 2 bits per node without analog trimming, and the node is ~1 nm thick instead of a ~1 um pillar.

title: Silicon interband tunnel-diode latch cell needing no refresh
idea: Worsen: make the cell need constant topping-up at 1 V or more. Flip: tie the storage node to a pair of series Si/SiGe resonant interband tunnel diodes whose negative differential resistance creates two stable node voltages, so the cell self-latches at ~0.3 V with pA standby current (tunneling SRAM revived with CMOS-compatible diodes).
why: Refresh energy and bandwidth tax disappear (fact 3); a 3x lower operating voltage cuts CV2 energy ~9x (fact 10); about one transistor plus two diodes per cell.

title: N: boron-alloyed AlN ferroelectric replaces the 70:1 capacitor pillar
idea: Use sputtered Al(1-x)B(x)N (no scandium), whose remanent polarization ~100-130 uC/cm2 is ~15-20x the charge density a linear DRAM dielectric holds at 1 V; a planar 40x40 nm capacitor switches ~3-4 fC, close to a 70:1 pillar's 5 fC, sensed as in 1T1C FeRAM.
why: Removes the high-AR pillar (fact 1) and its etch tools (fact 4); B, Al and N are abundant with U.S. boron; the high coercive field (~4-6 MV/cm) and fatigue must be engineered down.

title: Bone-marrow niche domain wall: conductive wall parked in pinning notch
idea: Long-lived plasma cells survive only in particular bone-marrow niches. Store the bit as whether a conductive ferroelectric domain wall sits in an engineered pinning 'niche', a notch in a thin-film LiNbO3 mesa between two read electrodes. A field pulse moves the wall in or out, and the wall's metallic conduction (10^3-10^6 on/off) is read non-destructively at low voltage.
why: Non-volatile, with non-destructive read, unlike FeRAM's destructive read (fact 8). ns switching, high endurance because no ions move, and US-producible LiNbO3.

title: Contact-free buckled nanotube bit clamped inside a BEOL via
idea: Invert 'storage is electronic' -> store the bit as which way a beam bows. A nanotube or nanowire clamped top and bottom in a BEOL via under compressive pre-strain buckles left or right; side electrodes flip it electrostatically and read the asymmetric capacitance, with no contact ever made, so no stiction or wear.
why: Non-volatile with zero leakage (fact 3), elastic bending can survive >1e15 cycles in principle, and it stacks in BEOL with no silicon transistor per bit (fact 2); thermal stability below 20 nm is the risk.

title: MLCC core-shell grain engineering for 5 nm high-k films
idea: Adapt the BaTiO3 core-shell grains MLCC makers use to flatten k versus field: grow nanolaminated rutile TiO2 grain cores with Al/Nb-doped shells via ALD supercycles, so k ~80-100 survives at 5 nm while grain-boundary leakage is blocked.
why: Fact 1: k ~70 is the stated escape route from the charge wall; ~1.6x Cs at the same AR, or today's Cs at AR ~45.

title: Bedouin's water-free release: XeF2-freed torsional NEMS seesaw bit
idea: A Bedouin wastes no water, and neither should the release step. A torsional nanopaddle tips to touch one of two landing electrodes and a small electrostatic bias holds it there; XeF2 vapor removes the sacrificial amorphous-silicon layer beneath it, eliminating HF wet release, DI rinses and critical-point drying.
why: A zero-leakage mechanical bit (facts 3, 9). Release, normally MEMS's most water-hungry step, uses no water, so the module needs more than 10x less UPW.

title: Liquid-nitrogen 77 K DRAM pods with planar capacitors
idea: Invert 'memory runs at room temperature' -> run DRAM at 77 K in liquid-nitrogen pods (nitrogen is abundant, unlike helium). Junction, GIDL and subthreshold leakage fall by >1e6, so a planar 0.3 fF capacitor retains for seconds, and steeper subthreshold slope allows ~0.6 V array and wordline swings.
why: Removes the capacitor charge wall (fact 1) and refresh (fact 3) and cuts CV^2 ~3x (fact 10); the ~10x cooling overhead at 77 K must be repaid by density and system energy gains.

title: Die-cast gallium droplet bit: liquid metal shuttles between two wells
idea: Borrow metal casting. A ~10 nm Ga-alloy droplet is sealed in a dumbbell-shaped nano-cavity, and electrocapillary pulses move it from one lobe to the other, where surface tension holds it (bistable). A sense electrode reads the position as a capacitance change.
why: Mechanical storage with no leakage, so no refresh (fact 3). A liquid cannot fatigue, so endurance is effectively unlimited and the state holds with no power.

title: H: bistable hydrogen site at Si/SiO2 interface as atomic bit
idea: Engineer a dense array of identical hydrogen defects that have two metastable configurations (bond-centred vs antibonding site, DX-like bistability); a field pulse moves the proton between sites, changing the local charge and a nearby nanowire's conductance.
why: The bit is one atom's position, giving density far beyond 6F² with no charge to leak (facts 1, 3, 4); reproducibility and room-temperature barrier height are speculative.

title: High-entropy fluorite oxide dielectric suppressing crystallization leakage paths
idea: Combine the high-entropy-alloy concept with the storage dielectric: an ALD supercycle mixes five cations (Hf, Zr, Ti, Ce, Sn) into one oxide so configurational entropy stabilizes a single fine-grained high-k phase and blocks the grain-boundary leakage paths that cripple pure TiO2 or ZrO2 at k>50. Target: k~50-60 with ZrO2-class leakage.
why: Facts 1 and 3: ~1.5x Cs at equal leakage and a tighter leakage tail; avoids scarce Ta, Nb and Ru.

title: Po: the bit is a shrug — sliding van der Waals ferroelectric
idea: Po: the bit is a shrug of the shoulders. Extracted: in bilayer hBN or rhombohedral MoS2 the bit is AB vs BA stacking; a field slides one layer by one bond length without breaking bonds, flipping polarization with almost no fatigue, read as a threshold shift of an underlying 2D channel.
why: Effectively unlimited endurance (no bond breaking, unlike HZO wake-up/fatigue) plus non-volatility. Wafer-scale stacking-controlled growth is the risk.

title: Bobeck bubble chip reborn: skyrmion minor loops with replicate gates
idea: Bring back the bubble chip's major/minor-loop organization (many short minor loops, transfer gates into a major loop) using 20-nm skyrmions in compensated ferrimagnetic GdFeCo stepped by spin-orbit-torque pulses. Keep the bubble chip's replicate gate, which splits a skyrmion and sends the copy to the detector, so reads are non-destructive.
why: At 40-nm pitch and ~1 bit/ns stepping a 32-bit minor loop gives <=32 ns access; only tracks are patterned so ~2F2 per bit, no capacitor or transistor per bit (Facts 1-4), non-volatile.

title: Nanoimprint-stamped capacitor pillar array instead of EUV
idea: Worsen: buy EUV exposures for every capacitor layer. Flip: because the capacitor array is a perfectly periodic hex lattice, write one master template by e-beam (~$150k) and replicate it by nanoimprint on a rented tool, demonstrating 30 nm-pitch capacitor holes on 200 mm test wafers within 18 months.
why: Capital and EUV intensity (fact 4): imprint is ~1/10 the cost per layer and removes the single-supplier EUV dependency for the storage array.

title: Optical Bragg mirror for electrons: superlattice blocks hold-state leakage
idea: Insert an epitaxial Si/SiGe (or AlGaN/GaN) superlattice into the storage-node leakage path designed so electrons at hold bias fall in a minigap and are Bragg-reflected, while at write bias a miniband aligns and transmits resonantly, making an electron energy filter that acts as a check valve.
why: Fact 3: suppresses band-to-band and trap-assisted tunneling (GIDL) at hold by ~100-1000x while keeping ns writes; coherent miniband transport through ~10 periods at room temperature is the physics risk.

title: Swap tungsten/platinum spin-orbit layer for chiral-molecule spin filter
idea: Write a nanomagnet bit by chiral-induced spin selectivity (CISS): a self-assembled monolayer of helical molecules (helicenes or alpha-helix peptides) spin-polarizes the write current, replacing heavy-metal W/Pt/Ta spin-orbit-torque layers.
why: Takes tungsten (China ~80%) and platinum-group metals out of non-volatile working memory, and the monolayer self-assembles with no lithography (scarce-resource axis).

title: Altermagnet RuO2 or MnTe bits with picosecond dynamics
idea: Jump to the picosecond timescale: altermagnets have zero net moment like antiferromagnets yet spin-split bands, so the Neel-vector bit is written by spin-orbit torque in ps and read by tunneling magnetoresistance, with no stray-field crosstalk.
why: Density and energy: no stray fields allows tight pitch; ps switching at low current.

title: Endohedral ion shuttle in a nanotube, adapted from e-paper
idea: Like E Ink moving charged pigment between two faces, trap a K+@C60 ion-fullerene inside a 3 nm capped carbon-nanotube segment; a field pulse slides it to one end, and its position changes tunneling current through the tube wall to a read electrode.
why: Density and fact 3: a ~5 nm two-state element held by van der Waals end-detents, with no charge-leakage path; predicted ps-ns switching.

title: Printed molecular-rotor framework where dipolar guests store the bit
idea: IFR: a crystal of identical, frictionless dipole switches. Closest achievable: print a metal-organic framework film whose pores hold polar rotor molecules that align up or down under a field and stay pinned by tuned ~0.8 eV rotational barriers, read as polarization charge.
why: Facts 1 and 10: molecular-scale bit with low switching barrier, printed from MOF inks at low temperature; no defect migration so endurance is high.

title: Microsecond-retention parasitic-node bit for streaming activations
idea: MINIFY retention on purpose from 64 ms to ~10 us: store bits only on the ~0.05 fF parasitic node of a capacitor-less vertical transistor and map the tier to AI activations and KV staging data that live < 10 us, so data is consumed before it decays and refresh never runs.
why: Drops capacitor and refresh (facts 1, 3); a transistor-only ~4F2 cell gives ~3x density for scratch buffers.

title: Four-shared readout cluster copied from smartphone camera pixels
idea: Adapt the 4-shared pixel: four tiny storage wells (~0.5 fF, no tall capacitor) share one floating diffusion and one source-follower gain transistor via four transfer gates, read one at a time with correlated double sampling.
why: Facts 1 and 7: drops the tall capacitor and amortizes readout to ~1.5 transistors per bit; ~1.5-2x density and non-destructive read.

title: Ferroelastic remanent-strain bit read by piezoresistive silicon nanowire
idea: Box = {medium: one of two remanent strain states from non-180-degree ferroelastic switching in a relaxor-PT film | access: Si FET | sense: piezoresistive Si nanowire under the film (gauge factor ~100+) | integration: BEOL with the nanowire channel below | substrate: Si | fab: sputter + rapid thermal anneal}. The bit is stored as lattice strain, not charge, and the nanowire's resistance differs by several percent between the two states; the read does not disturb the domains.
why: Facts 3 and 8: nonvolatile, nondestructive read, no restore, and no stored charge that can leak through a junction.

title: Pipe-organ multimode nanomechanical parametron with many bits per membrane
idea: Like one organ wind chest feeding many pipes, a single 100 nm membrane has ~100 vibrational modes; pump each mode parametrically at twice its frequency from a shared comb so each mode holds a 0/pi phase bit, read by heterodyne detection.
why: 10x at same cost: ~100 bits per 100x100 nm element is ~100 nm2/bit (~9x), and phase states never leak; pump-comb energy is the risk.

title: Hammer-triggered twin-cell mode doubles signal only where needed
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): the controller only issues ACT/REF/RFM as today. When the die's internal activation counter flags a row as an aggressor or victim, it silently remaps that row into twin-cell mode, storing each bit as a charge and its complement in two adjacent cells sensed differentially, which doubles signal and makes single-cell disturb flips harmless.
why: Neutralizes row hammer (fact 9) and weak-cell tails (fact 3) without host mitigation, and allows thinner cells elsewhere; spare rows absorb the small capacity cost.

title: Store the bit as a shape: snap-through buckled polysilicon beams
idea: Rearrange storage from charge to geometry: a compressively stressed 2 um polysilicon micro-bridge (1990s surface micromachining) buckles up or down; electrodes above and below snap it between states in ~50-100 ns and a capacitive pickoff reads the gap, with no contact so no stiction or wear.
why: Refresh (fact 3) and rad-hardness: zero-leakage nonvolatile storage with contactless (fatigue-limited only) cycling; ~4 um2/bit, so it targets harsh-environment and refresh-free buffers.

title: Swap charge for metastable charge-density-wave hidden state in 1T-TaS2
idea: A ~30 ps electrical pulse of ~fJ switches a nanoscale 1T-TaS2 cell from its insulating commensurate CDW into a metastable metallic hidden state, and a longer pulse resets it. The bit is the electronic order, read as a ~100x resistance ratio.
why: fJ, ps writes for the energy and speed axes. The hidden state is long-lived only below ~100 K, so this suits cryo AI racks or strain-stabilized films.

title: Revive deep-trench SOI eDRAM as U.S.-made memory chiplets
idea: Combine the deep-trench SOI eDRAM process once used in IBM POWER and z processors with chiplet and hybrid-bond stacking: a U.S. fab builds dense eDRAM-only chiplets on existing 14-22 nm SOI lines and stacks them into HBM-like cubes. Trench capacitors (~20-40 fF) are proven, and the lines are already depreciated.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital: domestic, EUV-free supply; large trench Cs also eases refresh; density ~1/4 of commodity DRAM but sovereign.

title: Traffic-jam phases: charge-density-wave domain states in 1T-TaS2
idea: Traffic flips between free flow and jams; in 1T-TaS2 electrons lock into commensurate or nearly commensurate charge-density-wave states with ~10x resistance contrast, and thin flakes switch between metastable states under short current pulses; build two-terminal cells from exfoliated ~10-nm flakes with e-beam contacts and hBN encapsulation.
why: A collective electronic state holds the bit with no ions or defects moving, so endurance could be effectively unlimited with fJ-scale switching; the narrow room-temperature metastability window threatens retention at 85 C.

title: Wide-bandgap charge well that never needs refresh
idea: IFR: a bit that holds itself forever with zero leakage. Closest achievable: store the bit as a deep-depletion charge well in a 4H-SiC (3.3 eV) MOS capacitor with a SiC access FET, where thermal generation scales as exp(-Eg/2kT) and falls by roughly 10^16x vs silicon, so retention moves from ms to hours.
why: Fact 3 (leakage tail/refresh): refresh energy and its 16-33% idle-power and 10-20% bandwidth tax go to near zero; with retention no longer limiting, Cs can shrink, easing fact 1.

title: Direct-tunnel germanium nanodot cell with seconds-long retention
idea: Worsen: force a choice between fast-but-leaky DRAM and slow-but-wearing flash. Flip: in a university cleanroom, grow Ge nanodots over a 1.5-2 nm tunnel oxide on standard MOSFETs so electrons tunnel directly in ~10 ns (no hot carriers, no wear) and the Ge band offset holds them for seconds.
why: Refresh cut ~100x versus 64 ms (fact 3) with non-destructive read; ~$400k of fab time.

title: Redox pseudocapacitor nanocell replaces 70:1 pillar with planar charge sponge
idea: Effect walk: Faradaic surface redox (pseudocapacitance). Replace the dielectric capacitor with a 5-nm hydrous RuO2 or Ti3C2 MXene film against a nanometre solid proton conductor; fast surface redox stores ~100-1000 uF/cm2 versus ~7 uF/cm2 for ZrO2, so a flat 30x30 nm pad holds ~4-5 fF at 0.5 V.
why: Breaks the capacitor charge wall (fact 1) with no AR 60-75 etch, removing the deep-etch/deposition module (~30-50% of capacitor cost); risks are self-discharge and whether surface redox keeps up at ns timescales.

title: Silicon-on-Nothing cavity tiers from MEMS pressure sensors
idea: Borrow MEMS pressure-sensor empty-space-in-silicon: H2-anneal trench arrays so silicon migrates into sealed buried voids, repeat to form 20 single-crystal Si membranes separated by voids, then fill the voids with ALD high-k/TiN as plate capacitors under single-crystal lateral transistors.
why: 10x at same cost: single-crystal tiers without SiGe superlattice epitaxy remove the 3D lateral-transistor quality blocker (fact 2); 20 tiers at relaxed DUV pitch, ~10x.

title: Eliminate the metal storage node: polyoxometalate clusters as multi-electron reservoirs
idea: Eliminate the electrode-plus-dielectric capacitor: graft one molybdenum- or vanadium-based polyoxometalate cluster per cell (no tungsten), which reversibly accepts 2-8 electrons at discrete, well-separated redox potentials, gated by an oxide-semiconductor access transistor; each redox state is one level, giving 2-3 bits per cell.
why: A 1-2 nm molecular storage node breaks the capacitor wall (fact 1) and multi-level raises density 2-3x; risks are redox kinetics under 10 ns and cycle endurance.

title: One hole mask defines every tier's annular capacitor in 3D
idea: Exascale machines need TB-class capacity; borrowing 3D NAND punch-and-plug, a single deep-hole mask through a 48-tier Si/SiGe stack is followed by lateral recess etches that carve an annular storage node and gate in every tier self-aligned to the hole, all tied to a shared vertical bitline.
why: Beats fact 2's 26+ tier break-even with only one critical mask for all tiers, collapsing litho cost per bit (fact 4); recess-etch uniformity across 48 tiers is the risk.

title: Po: the capacitor lies down and sleeps — flat pseudocapacitive tiers
idea: Po: the capacitor lies down and sleeps. Extracted: use a 5 nm MnO2 or Nb2O5 pseudocapacitive film (surface redox, 100s of uF/cm2) so a flat ~30x30 nm pad holds a few fF with no pillar; with each tier reduced to deposition plus one imprint, stack 32-64 tiers.
why: Removes the 60-75:1 etch (fact 1) and makes tiers cheap (fact 2); 64 flat tiers at relaxed pitch aim at 100x lower $/GB. Trade-offs: self-discharge, us redox kinetics, more frequent refresh.

title: Swap ZrO2 for high-entropy relaxor perovskite with k near 500
idea: Deposit a lead-free high-entropy relaxor such as (Ba,Sr)(Ti,Zr,Hf,Sn)O3, whose polar nanoregions give a slim, nearly linear loop and k ~300-800 in 15-20 nm films. Crystallize it by flash-lamp anneal to keep the CMOS below within its thermal budget.
why: ~10x k gives 5 fF from a 10:1 cap at 30-40 nm DUV pitch (facts 1, 4); entropy stabilization targets the leakage and thickness-scaling failures that ended 2000-era BST.

title: Segmented plate-line bootstraps stored charge for 0.4 V harvesters
idea: Thermoelectric-harvesting IoT runs at ~0.4 V; one cut mask splits the common capacitor plate into per-row plate lines so the selected row's plate is pulsed during read, bootstrapping the stored node ~2x before charge sharing. The bit is written at low array voltage yet read with a full-size signal.
why: Breaks the ~1 V VARY floor (fact 10) for ~4x lower CV2 write energy with one mask; plate-line drivers add periphery area (fact 7).

title: Eliminate plasma etch: metal-assisted chemical etching carves AR-150 capacitor holes
idea: Eliminate plasma etching: lay a perforated gold or silver catalyst mesh (nanoimprint lift-off or electroless plating) and immerse in HF/H2O2 at room temperature, so the catalyst sinks vertically and carves 25-nm holes in silicon at AR >150 with smooth walls in minutes; ALD liner and electrode turn the holes into capacitor shells.
why: Breaks the AR-75 ceiling (fact 1 asks for AR 115) without helium-cooled chucks or argon plasma, replacing a $10M+ etch tool with a wet bench (fact 4); risks are catalyst wandering and metal contamination.

title: Swap binary charge for eight-level charge with shared SAR sensing
idea: At relaxed DUV pitch (F ~ 20 nm) the larger cell cap stores eight charge levels (3 bits). They are read by a charge-redistribution SAR sense amplifier shared across four bitlines, protected by a strong symbol ECC, and refreshed at a rate set by the narrowest level margin.
why: 3 bits per cell offsets the ~2.8x area loss of skipping EUV (fact 4), giving equal or better bits per mm2 with no EUV capex.

title: Quantum-cascade-laser superlattice as a charge ladder per pillar
idea: Adapt QCL epitaxy: grow 8 coupled quantum wells with engineered barriers in each vertical pillar; each well's subband aligns with the injector at a unique bias, so resonant tunneling loads or senses one well at a time.
why: 10x at same cost: 8 wells x 2 levels in one 20 nm pillar footprint is ~16 bits, all defined by layer thickness in one epitaxy run rather than litho.

title: Dealloyed nanoporous electrode multiplies capacitor area tenfold
idea: IFR: infinite capacitor area in zero footprint. Closest achievable: deposit a binary alloy liner (e.g. Ag-Au or Al-Ti) in the pillar, selectively dissolve one metal to leave a nanoporous sponge electrode with ~5 nm ligaments, then ALD-coat dielectric and top electrode for 5-10x surface area.
why: Fact 1: 5 fF at AR ~20 instead of 60-75; shorter deep etches cut tool time and capital (fact 4).

title: Lighthouse keeper: photonic-crystal nanocavity optical bistable bit
idea: A lighthouse keeper stores the message in the beam itself. Each bit is an InP photonic-crystal nanocavity held in one of two optically bistable states by a shared ~uW holding laser; femtojoule pulses on a waveguide write and read it, as a buffer co-packaged with optical I/O.
why: Attacks data-movement energy (fact 5) by keeping data optical between links, with no electrical charge to leak.

title: UV-C LED AlGaN ultra-wide-bandgap capacitorless node in tiers
idea: Borrow AlGaN from UV-C LED fabs: a ~6 eV bandgap AlGaN channel transistor with near-zero leakage holds charge on its own gate node (no capacitor) for hours, enabling a 4F2 2T0C cell stacked in 8 low-temperature-deposited tiers.
why: 10x at same cost: no capacitor and no refresh, 1.5x from 4F2 x 8 tiers is ~12x; nitride tools are mature and present in the US.

title: Bistable buckled nanobeam storing bits as mechanical position
idea: Combine a pre-compressed (buckled) SiC nanobeam, which has two stable shapes, with a capacitive-gap read: an electrostatic pulse snaps the beam up or down, and the beam's position sets the capacitance to a sense electrode. Mechanical bistability holds the bit with zero hold current and no refresh; nanoscale beams switch in ~10 ns.
why: Facts 3 and 9: refresh (16-33% of idle power) and row hammer both disappear because there is no charge to leak or disturb; SiC MEMS show >1e12-cycle fatigue life.

title: Electrolytic-capacitor memory: pseudocapacitive planar cell beats the pillar wall
idea: Early electrolytic storage used electrochemical double layers for enormous capacitance. Deposit ALD hydrous RuO2 or MnO2 with a solid proton-conducting electrolyte as a planar storage capacitor on an existing 65/90-nm logic flow, reaching ~5 fF in ~0.05 um2 with no high-aspect-ratio etch.
why: Attacks the charge wall (Fact 1) with ~100x capacitance density and skips the 60:1 pillar etch (Fact 4 capex); risks are ns-scale ion response and self-discharge.

title: Eliminate destructive read: erasable conductive ferroelectric domain walls as bits
idea: Eliminate charge-sharing readout: in single-crystal LiNbO3 thin-film nanocells, a field pulse writes or erases a charged, conducting domain wall bridging two side electrodes in ns; reading is a small current through the wall (on/off ~1e3) that leaves the polarization undisturbed.
why: Non-destructive read removes the 128x overfetch and restore cost (fact 8) and refresh (fact 3); risks are scaling below 20 nm and wall-pinning variation.
